title: Making the Grade (But Not Disclosing It): How Withholding Grades Affects Student Behavior and Employment
authors: Eric Floyd; Sorabh Tomar; Daniel J. Lee
eligible_reason: Tables 7 and 8 (main text, actual data) estimate felm(y ~ gnd | educYearStart + nyu, cluster = school x cohort) on MBA graduates of Columbia and NYU, with gnd switching on for Columbia entering cohorts from 2011 and NYU cohorts from 2013 (code.R line 702 comment; confirmed in shipped educ/emp: first gnd cohort 2011 for nyu==FALSE, 2013 for nyu==TRUE, absorbing). Two adoption cohorts, NYU 2011-2012 is the not-yet-treated comparison, school and cohort-year FE, no controls, no weights. Repeated cross-sections assigned to stable groups (schools).
design_notes: R (lfe, data.table). data.rdata holds educ (1,272 Columbia/NYU MBA profiles, cohorts 2000-2018: id, nyu, educYearStart, educYearEnd, act, gnd) and emp (9,287 job rows). Table 7: extracurricular engagement. Table 8: first-job tenure, samples truncated at 2016/2015/2014/2013 to avoid censoring. Re-estimated with fixest from the shipped data (scratch check): all 8 coefficients, SEs and Ns match the log exactly (T7: 0.076/0.032, 0.324/0.193, 0.135/0.044, N=1,272, 38 clusters; T8: -0.077/0.010 N=601, -0.128/0.038 N=547, 0.029/0.035 N=456, -0.096/0.033 N=404, -0.311/0.093 N=404). The paper's headline analyses (Tables 1-6, Figures 1-4) study one field-site business school that adopted grade non-disclosure in 2001 (full-time vs part-time students; single date; GPA interactions) and ship synthetic data only.
main_or_robustness: secondary (main-text extension to Columbia/NYU; headline field-site design is single-date)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Columbia 2011, NYU 2013 (entering-cohort years). No never-treated school: after 2013 every cohort is treated. CSA (not-yet-treated) identifies only ATT(2011, 2011-2012); the NYU cohort has no comparison. BJS can impute Y(0) only for treated cells in 2011-2012 (year FE for 2013+ have no untreated rows). Coverage: educ 68 of 845 treated rows (8%); Table 8 col 1 sample 54 of 304 (18%); cols 4-5 54 of 107 (50%). Report BJS/CSA coverage per 5b.

data_files_note: code.R header and README: Tables 1-6 and Figures 1-4 use confidential data replaced by synthetic data; Tables 7-9 use the actual public-profile data (educ, emp), with employer/position recoded to numbers for confidentiality. The construction of educ/emp from the primary profile tables is shown as commented code.
data_provenance_note: Original for the eligible specs (Tables 7-8, reproduced exactly). Synthetic for the ineligible Tables 1-6; do not add this paper to synthetic_packages.txt on that basis.
screener_notes: Eligible but thin: 2 assignment units (schools), 38 school x cohort clusters, no never-treated unit, and from 2013 on every observation is treated, so TWFE leans on already-treated Columbia cohorts as controls for NYU. Modern estimators are identified only for Columbia's 2011-2012 cohorts. Expect large TWFE-vs-modern gaps and low BJS/CSA coverage; the leverage screen (effective clusters, max cluster share) should be checked at the cluster level used. Table and column locations come from code labels (no article text available); re-check against the published PDF.
